entry.label: Feedback
entry.description: A family of circular causal or informational relations in which consequences return to influence later state or action. Its sign, delay, reference condition, mechanism and response capacity must be stated.
entry.canonical_definition: A circular causal or informational relation in which an output or consequence affects later input, state or action. The sign, delay, reference condition and mechanism must be stated.

profile.title: Feedback
profile.canonical_definition: A circular causal or informational relation in which an output or consequence affects later input, state or action. The sign, delay, reference condition and mechanism must be stated.
profile.summary: Feedback is not merely receiving comments. It is a circular relation in which consequences return to influence what happens next. The loop may counteract change, reinforce it, oscillate, delay response or fail because no actor can use the returned information.
profile.why_it_matters: Systems work often says feedback when it means reporting, evaluation, data or learning. Those are only feedback when they close a loop that can alter subsequent action. Sign, delay, reference condition and response capacity determine what the loop actually does.
key_distinctions: negative or balancing vs positive or reinforcing feedback
feedback signal vs capacity to respond
physical causal loop vs returned information
historical_lineage: Maxwell 1868: mathematical governor analysis as a precursor
Rosenblueth, Wiener and Bigelow 1943: purposive behaviour and negative feedback
Wiener 1948: cybernetic synthesis across animals and machines
logical_antecedents: a return path through which consequences can alter later conditions
a reference or viability condition where correction is claimed
practice_connections: ask what information returns to whom
test whether anyone can alter action in response
state the delay before effects become visible
look for loops that reward gaming rather than purpose
common_misreadings: positive means good and negative means bad
a dashboard is feedback even when nobody can act
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.

claims.statement: Maxwell's 'On Governors' is a historical precursor to later mathematical feedback and control analysis; this does not imply that Maxwell used the later cybernetic concept or terminology.

claims.statement: Positive and negative feedback name the sign and effect of a loop, not whether the result is morally or practically good or bad.
claims.notes: Core orientation claim for non-specialist readers.

claims.statement: Feedback is a definitional prerequisite for Wiener's 1948 formulation of cybernetics, while later cybernetics may frame the field more broadly.

sources.title: On Governors
sources.notes: James Clerk Maxwell, Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, vol. 16, pp. 270–283. Bibliographic records span 1867–1868. Used here as a historical precursor to mathematical analysis of governors and control; it does not use the later cybernetic vocabulary of feedback.

sources.title: Stabilized Feedback Amplifiers
sources.notes: H. S. Black, Bell System Technical Journal 13(1), pp. 1–18. Primary engineering account of the negative-feedback amplifier principle. The invention predates the paper; this release does not make a first-invention claim.

sources.title: Behavior, Purpose and Teleology
sources.notes: Arturo Rosenblueth, Norbert Wiener and Julian Bigelow, Philosophy of Science 10(1), pp. 18–24. Primary pre-cybernetics article connecting purposive behaviour with input/output relations and negative feedback.

sources.title: Cybernetics or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
sources.notes: Norbert Wiener's foundational synthesis, first published in 1948. The MIT Press open-access reissue describes feedback and information as central to the field. Exact chapter-level use remains a next editorial check.
